---
title: "Session files"
---

PMV 1.5.6 introduces a new session file. It no longer relies on log strings and on playing back
the entire session, which was error prone and slow.

The new session file is self-contained: you can send it to another user and it restores the
session. It contains a Python script that issues all the PMV commands needed to create the
molecular geometries and configure them as they were when the session was saved. Vision networks
are saved and restored too.

Session files are gzipped tar files with the extension `.psf` (PMV Session File).

::: {.callout-note}
## Limitations
- Molecules read from PDBQ, PDBQT and PDBQS files are saved in their original format. All other
  molecules are currently saved as PDB files, which can lose information (for example from mol2
  files).
- Only `ATOM`, `HETATM` and `CONECT` records are saved for molecules in a session file. For
  example, a molecule read from a PDB file with secondary structure records loses these records
  when restored from a session, so its secondary structure is assigned programmatically and may
  differ from the PDB records.
- Some representations are not restored: splines, CA traces, distance, angle and torsion
  measurements, and isosurfaces of volumetric data.
- Geometry not created by PMV (for example created in Vision) is not restored.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Known bug
PMV molecules used in Vision networks are not restored.
:::
